text:
maria: AcmeCorp reported intermittent 503s around 03:20 UTC. They sent two request IDs they saw in their client logs: req_8f3a2b and req_8f3a9f. They also asked for a reproducible curl and said they can't share full prompts w/PII. Need guidance on collecting a debug bundle and how we should pseudonymize prompt content before ingesting.
ops-bot: Ticket created: SUP-2026-411. Assigned to @jordan.
jordan: Thanks — can someone grab a sanitized curl reproducer + the server-side request IDs, and the inference node logs for the window 2026-03-15T03:15:00Z -> 03:30:00Z? Also include the model + route used and the exact X-Request-ID headers. If they can run a curl that hits the same code path that triggered the 503 that helps a lot.
alex: For logs I can export pod logs and search for the request IDs. Will need the cluster+namespace: inference-prod, team: redwood-serving. I'll pull them and redact auth headers before we attach.
maria: @sara, can you confirm the scrub checklist so we don't accidentally keep PII? We need to provide the customer with clear steps they can run locally to pseudonymize prompts before sending us the bundle.
sara: Here's a minimal, defensive checklist I recommend. Share this with the customer and ask them to confirm before uploading.
Checklist (short):
1) Replace full email addresses with <EMAIL>
2) Hash or truncate user IDs (keep first 6 chars, then replace rest with <UID>)
3) Replace phone and SSN-like patterns with <SENSITIVE_NUM>
4) Remove API keys, session tokens, cookies — replace with <REDACTED_TOKEN>
5) If a prompt contains long PII-rich history, replace entire history with a short pseudonymized summary
6) Keep timestamps and request IDs intact (we need them for correlation)
Examples (shareable commands):
```bash
# basic sed-based email/phone scrub
sed -E 's/[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}/<EMAIL>/g; s/\b[0-9]{3}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{4}\b/<SENSITIVE_NUM>/g' raw_prompts.txt > sanitized_prompts.txt

# hash user ids (sha1 first 6 chars + marker)
cat user_ids.txt | while read id; do echo "$(printf \"%s\" \"$id\" | sha1sum | cut -c1-6)-<UID>"; done > hashed_user_ids.txt
```
jordan: Nice. For curl reproducer please use the sanitized body and remove the Authorization header. Example we can give them:

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: req_8f3a2b" \
  -d '{"model": "gpt-infer-01", "input": "<SANITIZED_PROMPT>", "max_tokens": 64}'
```
leo: Customer asked if they can just upload a debug bundle to S3. Yes — provide them a one-time pre-signed URL. But require they follow the checklist and include a short manifest file mapping original request IDs -> sanitized filenames.
maria: I'll create a presigned S3 url and send instructions. Action items:
- alex: export logs for the window and scrub sensitive env lines before upload (I'll give you ACL to the debug bucket). (Due: +1h)
- jordan: prepare the correlation script that maps X-Request-ID -> internal trace ids and include it in the bundle. (Due: +2h)
- sara: review the customer's sanitized files once uploaded to verify no raw emails/SSNs remain before we open case materials. (Due: when uploaded)
- leo: confirm you sent the presigned URL + checklist to the customer and get back when they upload. (Due: +30m)
alex: Got it, starting log export now. I'll run a quick grep for req_8f3a2b and req_8f3a9f and redact Authorization headers with: `perl -pe 's/Authorization:.*$/Authorization: <REDACTED_TOKEN>/'` before packaging.
sara: If you want a stricter scrub, use our redaction script (internal):
```bash
python tools/redact_bundle.py --input bundle.tar.gz --email-mask '<EMAIL>' --token-mask '<REDACTED_TOKEN>' --phone-mask '<SENSITIVE_NUM>' --output bundle.sanitized.tar.gz
```
I'll validate the sanitized tarball once it's uploaded to the secure bucket.
maria: Perfect. I'll DM the presigned URL and checklist, and tag this thread when upload completes.
leo: Sent to customer — they confirmed they will sanitize and upload in ~20m.
maria: Thanks all — keep updates here. If we get a sanitized curl that reproduces the 503, attach it to the ticket with the X-Request-ID header unchanged so we can correlate with traces.
